24_marg506: In the days of Assuerus. Rabanus. The book of Esther, which the Hebrews number among the Hagiographa, contains the sacraments of Christ and the Church. For Esther, in figure of the Church, frees the people from danger, and, Aman (which is interpreted “iniquity”) being slain, hands down to posterity the portions of the feast and a solemn day.
24_marg507: We do not doubt that the history of Esther was in the time of Assuerus, but who Assuerus was we do not know. Josephus, however, records that he was Cyrus, the son of Xerxes, who ruled the empire of Persia after his father Darius. He said that this Cyrus is called Artaxerxes among the Greeks, who, surnamed Longhand, reigned forty years; but Esther does not seem to have lived at that time, for perhaps Esdras would not have passed her over, who wove the history of the things done when the captives returned from Babylon to Jerusalem. But Eusebius in his Chronicles judges that this is the Artaxerxes who is surnamed Memnon, the son of Darius and Parysatis. He is called Assuerus by the Hebrews, Artaxerxes by the Seventy interpreters, and reigned forty years after Darius, surnamed Nothus.
24_marg508: Susa is the chief city in Persia, which the historians say Memnon’s brother founded, and that it took its name from the river Susis. There is the royal house of Cyrus, of white and varied stone, with golden pillars and ceilings set off with gems, containing an image of the heavens marked with twinkling stars, and many incredible things. There Assuerus held a very great feast, with riches and an abundance of delights. For the power of the sacred word sometimes so tells things past as to express things to come; so approves the doer as to gainsay him in his ministry; so condemns deeds done as to urge that they be done mystically.
24_interl1409: Assuerus, namely, who shows Christ by name and dignity; for he is interpreted “my court” or “door”. And Christ says: “I am the door of the sheep”, etc.
24_marg509: In the time, namely, of this world he laid open the sacrament of his incarnation, and served most abundantly the spiritual feasts of preaching and of his body and blood. The first time is before the law, the second under the law, the third under grace.
24_marg510: A great feast. “The kingdom of heaven is likened to a king, who made a marriage for his son.” And elsewhere: “A certain man made a great supper, and invited many.”
24_marg511: The history of this feast shows the pomp of riches and the luxury of the king, but allegorically it signifies the spiritual delights of Christ, which he deals out to each. For Christ is that most rich king, who, moved by the prayers of his wife, that is, the Church, frees his own, that is, his confessors, from the hand of the enemies, and condemns those justly. For it is not necessary that, if the good things of some signify Christ, their evil things too should fit Christ himself. For Moses signified Christ in many things, but not in this, that he doubted at the waters of contradiction; nor Aaron in the making of the calf, nor Solomon in the filth of lust. So Assuerus in this judgement, as in the liberal feast, signifies Christ; as Isaias signifies Christ in Cyrus, king of the Persians, of whom he afterwards adds: “I girded thee, and thou hast not known me”, etc. For if wicked kings in their misdeeds signify the devil, why should not just kings in their good deeds show forth Christ? Nabuchodonosor commanded the peoples, when they heard the sound of the symphony and the music, to fall down and adore the statue; and the devil, by worldly sweetness, bends the human race from uprightness of mind to follow covetousness, which is the service of idols.

24_marg515: That is, the teachers, of whom it is said: “I have established the pillars thereof.” And elsewhere: “The pillars thereof he made of silver, the seat of gold.”

24_marg535: The powerful of the world, who, abusing the benefits conferred by the divine power, scorn to have as sharers of grace those whom they have as sharers of nature, and strive to transfer to themselves the honour and reverence which they owed to God alone. And those who will not consent they pursue with hatreds and torments; but by the just judgement of God the wicked are caught in their own snares. Whence it is said: “The just is delivered out of distress: and the wicked shall be given up for him.” By Aman, whom Josephus records to be of the stock of Amalec, the people of the Jews can be figured, who slew the prophets and the Lord of the prophets and his apostles, losing the nobility of their race through unbelief and hardness of heart; who by Isaias are called “ye rulers of Sodom … ye people of Gomorrha”. 24_marg549: Make haste. They mount upon the king’s horse, that is, upon the faithful people, in whose hearts the King of angels dwells. Whence the prophet Habacuc: “Who will ride upon thy horses: and thy chariots are salvation.” To them Aman, the special enemy of the people of God, pays service, though against his will, when the persecutors of the Church are compelled to bear witness to that same Church, unable to hide what is plain.
24_marg550: So Aman took, etc. This is the change of the right hand of the most High: he who seemed to himself the more glorious appears below others, viler and lower; according to that: “He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble.” Likewise Isaias says: “Libanus shall be turned into charmel, and charmel shall be esteemed as a forest.” So the pride of the Synagogue was crushed, the humility of the Church exalted. So the persecutors of the faith were brought to nothing, the confessors of Christ exalted in the whole world. The head was turned into the tail and the tail into the head, because everyone “that exalteth himself shall be humbled”.
24_interl1684: for often worldly men, being converted, understand and confess the truth
24_marg551: So … went in, etc. On the second day of the feast Aman came, invited. But when Esther opened her request, he went out condemned to punishment. For in the gospel a dinner and a supper are mentioned. The dinner signifies the present time of the Church; the supper, the eternal and last feast. Whence, the wicked being separated, the good rejoice for ever. For Aman, because he had not a garment worthy of the feast, deserved to be cast out.
24_marg552: As the king hastens into the garden, that is, invites the elect with him to the delights of paradise, he strives to entreat the queen for his life, but had not a fitting time. For the remedies of salvation are sought too late when the dangers of death are at hand. Whence Solomon: “Then shall they call upon me, and I will not hear: they shall rise in the morning, and shall not find me.”
24_interl1687: confusion and shame, according to that: “Let them be clothed with confusion and shame, that desire evils to me”

24_marg554: He signifies the teachers of the law, who foretold the crimes and deceits of the Jews. 24_interl1688: “He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that rolleth a stone, it shall return to him”

24_marg571: Now the thirteenth day, etc. Note that some of the Jews kill on the thirteenth day and leave off on the fourteenth and keep the solemnity; some kill for two days, that is, the thirteenth and fourteenth day of the same month, and rest solemnly on the fifteenth. For some of the saints, after finishing the labours by which they serve God by believing well and living well, now, before the time of judgement, have in their souls the sabbath of everlasting rest. Others, lasting on in the flesh until the last day of the resurrection, having overcome all their enemies and being suddenly changed, receive the rest of souls and bodies. Whence the Apostle: “The dead who are in Christ, shall rise first. Then we who are alive, who are left, shall be taken up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ, into the air”, etc. For the fourteenth, which contains twice seven, signifies the perfect rest of souls; but the fifteenth, embracing seven and eight, signifies the rest of souls and bodies.
